overview: Kyrgyzstan is a landlocked, mountainous country in Central Asia. Its capital and largest city is Bishkek. Kyrgyzstan became independent from the Soviet Union in 1991. Many Kyrgyz people were traditionally nomadic herders, and yurts and horses are still important in the country's culture.

geography.text: Most of Kyrgyzstan is covered by the Tian Shan and Pamir mountain ranges, and nearly all of it lies more than 1,000 metres above sea level. Issyk-Kul in the north-east is one of the largest mountain lakes in the world and does not freeze in winter. The fertile Fergana Valley lies in the south-west.

subsections.title: Climate
subsections.text: Cold winters and warm summers, with mountain weather in most of the country.

subsections.title: Wildlife
subsections.text: Snow leopards, Marco Polo sheep and golden eagles.

history.text: Kyrgyz people have lived as herders in the Tian Shan mountains for centuries, and the Silk Road passed through the region. Russia took control in the 1800s, and it became a Soviet republic. Kyrgyzstan became independent in 1991, and protests have toppled its government several times since.

events.title: Russian conquest
events.text: The region is absorbed into the Russian Empire.

events.title: Soviet republic
events.text: Kirghizia becomes a full Soviet republic.

government.text: Kyrgyzstan is a presidential republic. Protests have toppled presidents three times, in 2005, 2010 and 2020. A new constitution in 2021 strengthened the President's powers.

economy.text: Gold mining is Kyrgyzstan's biggest export industry, and money sent home by Kyrgyz workers in Russia makes up a large share of the economy. Farming, especially herding, is also important.

culture.text: More than 90% of Kyrgyzstan is mountainous. Nomadic traditions remain strong, including yurts, felt carpets and horse games. The Epic of Manas, one of the longest poems in the world, is recited by storytellers called manaschi.

items.title: Epic of Manas
items.text: An oral poem hundreds of thousands of lines long.

items.title: Issyk-Kul
items.text: A huge mountain lake that never freezes.

items.title: Kalpak
items.text: A tall white felt hat worn by men.

subsections.title: Food
subsections.text: Beshbarmak and kymyz, fermented mare's milk.

subsections.title: Music and arts
subsections.text: The Manas epic and the komuz, a three-stringed lute.

subsections.title: Traditions and festivals
subsections.text: Shepherds take their animals to summer pastures, living in yurts.

sport.text: Kyrgyzstan hosts the World Nomad Games, featuring traditional sports such as kok-boru, a horseback game with a goat carcass. Wrestling has brought Olympic medals.

items.title: World Nomad Games
items.text: Started in Kyrgyzstan in 2014 and held there again in 2016 and 2018.

items.title: Kok-boru
items.text: Horseback teams fight over a goat carcass.
